subject.title: Multi-agent orchestration is unstable: concurrent agents add/config overwrites, session-lock failures, and detached child work

question: Should this issue remain the canonical umbrella while focused session-lock and delivery fixes land, or should maintainers replace it with a narrower canonical design issue for multi-agent completion isolation?
rationale: The source and discussion show real remaining failures, but the durable solution crosses session ownership, completion payload policy, fallback-lane behavior, and cancellation semantics that require maintainer product intent.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Focused Fixes
options.body: Keep this issue open, review focused work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86540 individually, and close only after linked lock, delivery, fallback, auth-noise, and detached-work symptoms are resolved or explicitly split.

options.title: Promote Completion Isolation Design
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96975 the canonical product direction and map remaining bug reports to that design before closing this umbrella.

options.title: Split By Root Cause
options.body: Select one canonical issue per root cause and close this umbrella only after each production-evidence thread is linked to its owner.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Land Focused Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, review focused work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/86540 individually, and close only after linked lock, delivery, fallback, auth-noise, and detached-work symptoms are resolved or explicitly split.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is primarily the product/architecture boundary for core agent orchestration and session ownership, and steipete has the strongest recent history across the relevant agent runtime surface.
